items.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021
items.q: as a teenager I’m listening to Cannonball and John Coltrane. So when I would get on the job I would be ready to stretch out.

ctx.x: So at what point did you get the idea, or were you forced into, being an improviser?

It was automatic. Because I heard music from the womb. In other words I heard, my mother played piano up until the say I was born, you know playing at the local Moose Club or something like that and she’s pregnant. And so I literally, and I have no documentation, but I pretty much learned the American Songbook in the womb. And improvisation, naturally when I started listening to, when I started playing and listening to records and understood what improvisation was, right away, say for instance I’m listening, as a…
It’s interesting you say that because I was listening to your recording of “For All We Know” and it was simply gorgeous.
